subtitle: Lime-cured fish on crisp tostadas
verso: Lime, fish and a tostada: the beach, and it costs you nothing.
story: On the Mexican coast, ceviche is fish cured in lime until white, then mixed with tomato, onion, cilantro and chile and piled on a crisp tostada with avocado and hot sauce. In Acapulco it gets a splash of catsup; in Sinaloa, cucumber, carrot and a swipe of mayonnaise.

ingredients.title: The fish
items: 1 lb very fresh firm white fish (sierra, mahi-mahi, snapper or tilapia), finely diced

steps: Put the fish in a glass bowl with the salt and enough lime juice to cover. Refrigerate 30–40 minutes, stirring once, until the fish is white all the way through.
Drain off most of the lime juice.
Fold in the tomato, onion, serrano, cilantro and cucumber. Taste for salt.
Spread each tostada thinly with mayonnaise if you like, pile on the ceviche and top with avocado and hot sauce.
pressureNote: No pressure-cooker version. The lime cooks the fish.
tips: Cut the fish small and even so it all cures at the same time.
Use a glass or ceramic bowl, not metal, for the lime.
Very fresh fish only. Raw seafood isn't for pregnant women or small children.

variations.name: Ceviche de Camarón
variations.subtitle: Shrimp ceviche
variations.note: With shrimp instead of fish, cured raw like aguachile or poached a minute first.

items: 1 lb shrimp, peeled, deveined and chopped
The tomato, onion, serrano, cilantro and cucumber from the base

steps: Cure the shrimp in the lime juice 20 minutes in the fridge, or poach them 1 minute and chill them first.
Drain and fold in the vegetables and carrot.
